prompt: Across an ideal fixed-voltage supply, you first add a second positive resistor in series with an existing resistor, then try it as a parallel branch instead. How does total supply current change?

options.text: Series reduces it; adding a parallel branch increases it
options.explanation: Correct. Series adds resistance to one path; parallel adds another path drawing current.

options.text: Series increases it; parallel reduces it
options.explanation: This reverses the effect of an added restriction versus an added path.
A parallel branch adds supply current while the original branch keeps the same voltage.
A fixed supply voltage does not imply a fixed total current.

workedExample: In series every charge path includes both resistors, so the equivalent resistance rises and current falls. In parallel the original resistor still has the same voltage, while the new branch draws additional current. The prediction assumes the supply holds its voltage rather than sagging or entering current limit.
